claims.text: The initial FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size distribution of 15–45 μm.
Binder-assisted agglomeration under low-oxygen conditions can convert the 15–45 μm feedstock into 50–100 μm granules.
Approximately 1–2 wt% volatile organic binder is an appropriate concentration for the proposed agglomeration.
Minor adjustments to plasma temperature or substrate preheating can ensure thorough binder burnout during flight.
The agglomerated feedstock forms larger molten droplets during APS deposition.
Larger molten droplets provide higher deposited mass per splat.
An inert agglomeration atmosphere and controlled thermal profile minimize oxidation and binder residue.
Minimized oxidation and binder residue enhance splat coalescence and produce a denser lamellar structure.
The temporary binder coating shields individual FeCoNiCrAl particles from oxidation during APS flight.
The binder volatilizes completely at APS temperatures.
Binder burnout yields larger, uniformly molten particles.
The larger molten particles form thicker, well-adhered splats.
Binder-assisted agglomeration increases APS deposition efficiency.
Binder-assisted agglomeration produces a coating significantly thicker than the coating produced from the 15–45 μm baseline feedstock.
The resulting bond coat has a uniform lamellar microstructure with minimal oxidation.
The resulting bond coat has adequate mechanical adhesion for use in a thermal barrier coating system.
The standard 15–45 μm-feedstock APS process produces insufficient coating thickness and some oxidation.
The intervention remains effective under standard APS configurations and typical TBC service conditions when binder concentration, atmosphere, and thermal parameters are controlled.

contradictions.description: The intervention calls for optimized or adjusted APS thermal parameters, while the experiment requires identical APS parameters for both groups. If both groups receive the optimized settings, the control is not the stated standard-APS baseline; if only the agglomerated group receives them, the APS parameters are not identical.
